findings.locator: tools/textbook-relation-decisions-r7.json batch_rejection_rewrites[*].restored_r6_comparison_text / rejection_reason (indices 10-19, 49-52, 76-82, 157-163, 212-218, 297-305, 331-335, 381-385, 390-396 and others); analysis/textbook-exam-relations-r7.json (71 rejected rows); analysis/objective-problem-map.json (11 distinct fragments)
findings.expected: Restore the R6 comparison text, dropping only the batch phrase and keeping its meaning. 'None of these targets asks for X' should become 'This exam part does not ask for X', or the sentence should be dropped.
findings.actual: In 72 of the 77 records whose R6 reason contains 'None of these targets ...', the phrase was replaced by an affirmative lowercase 'this exam part ...' (asks 37, requires 17, requests 7, credits 6, uses 5). The negation is inverted. Example: 2021 P1 Q8(b) / ap-index-and-membership now reads 'this exam part asks for an AP term position or membership verdict'. The exam actually asks for the constant increase A, and the next sentence of the same reason says so. Another example: 2021 P2 Q6(b) / special-angle-connected-geometry reads 'this exam part requires that length-recovery/triangle connection'. 71 current ledger rejection reasons and 11 distinct fragments in objective-problem-map.json carry the inverted text. In addition, 84 reasons now contain a lowercase 'this exam part' after a full stop.
findings.evidence: A python comparison of r6_rejection_reason with restored_r6_comparison_text across all 403 records. check_repair_r7_closeout.py only asserts that restored_r6_comparison_text appears in rejection_reason and that the batch phrase is absent; check_repair_r7.py:24 forbids 'none of these targets', which pushed the substitution.
findings.repair: Regenerate these 72 with 'This exam part does not <verb> ...' (or remove that sentence), capitalise the sentence starts, re-propagate to the ledger and the map, and add a negative fixture that fails when an R6 'None of these targets' sentence becomes an affirmative 'this exam part' clause. The decisions themselves are unchanged and the text stays non-evidence (template status).

findings.branch: exponential-scale-context-support vs 8227:EXAM:2021:P2:Q4:b (Goldie 2B Q14(iii) mixed; 2B Q13(ii,iii) rejected)
findings.locator: analysis/textbook-exam-relations-r7.json relation exponential-scale-context-support / 2021:P2:Q4:b differing_decision; member_level_exceptions f585478db35f4c64f67e rejection_reason; checks/repair-r7-closeout.md R7-03 table
findings.expected: The exam-side difference used to set the branch direction should agree with the official marking. The project already records the conflict as 8227:CONVENTION:009: the report prose says 34 complete weeks, but the award row accepts 35.
findings.actual: The reason says the exam 'asks full weeks, so it requires floor rather than nearest rounding' and uses that 'full-week boundary' to make the branch mixed. The Richter rejection also cites a 'discrete-time boundary'. The award row on report PDF 238 reads 't = 34 ... A1 Accept: 35', and 35 is the nearest-integer rounding of 34.657, so the floor-versus-nearest distinction is not enforced by the marking. The same reason also begins 'Both solve a supplied exponential-scale relation' and then says the source 'constructs the offset equation', which contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: Rendered NSSCAS_2021_Examiners.pdf PDF 238 and 2021 P2 PDF 6; analysis/marking-conventions.json 8227:CONVENTION:009.
findings.repair: Cite CONVENTION:009 and state the boundary as 'complete weeks: 34; award also accepts 35'. Then re-judge the direction. With the source constructing its own scale equation and the exam supplying a ready model, the source is probably the harder side. Otherwise name a valid exam-side extra if mixed is kept. Adjust the Richter rejection wording the same way; that rejection stands on its other grounds.

findings.branch: BP-09 and BP-27 (same type) and BP-08 (harder) against 8227:EXAM:2023:P2:Q9:b
findings.locator: analysis/textbook-exam-relations-r7.json rows sample_id BP-08, BP-09, BP-27; checks/repair-r7-closeout.md R7-01 table
findings.expected: Same type is judged per matched part, including the direct-demand set, and one rule is applied across the close-out. The direct demands of 2023 P2 Q9(b) include 8227:2020:M2:T5:O01:D01 (integrate e^(ax+b)). YM Ex38(d) and Try Now 39 Q1(c) integrate polynomials only.
findings.actual: BP-09 and BP-27 are labelled same type, and BP-08 'harder', treating polynomial versus exponential integrand as surface variation. A coverage_caveat records that the polynomial primitive does not practise the exam's exponential integration. In the same close-out, BP-24 and BP-31 count an absent exponential/product derivative as a reason the textbook is easier. The motion labels therefore follow a different rule from the curve labels. The objective map is not inflated: its demand_link_basis does not credit M2:T5:O01:D01 to these families, and the other same-type and branch rows for 2023 P2 Q9(b) already cover exponential primitives as easier branches.
findings.evidence: Rendered YM 364/366/368 and 2023 P2 PDF 15; question-analysis.json directly_assessed_demand_ids for 2023:P2:Q9:b; objective-problem-map.json entry for M2:T5:O01:D01.
findings.repair: Either relabel BP-09/BP-27 as structural branch (easier) and BP-08 as mixed, or state the rule ('function family alone is not a learner decision') explicitly and make the coverage caveat binding, so that step 3 never cites these polynomial items as same-type practice for the exponential-integration demand. BP-38 and BP-22 (polynomial on both sides) are correctly same type.
